paragraphs: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi, student of Rav, Shmuel, and Zeira. During the falling-on-the-face prayer he would regularly say, “May the Merciful One save me from the evil inclination.” His wife said, “But he has withdrawn from me”—because of old age, according to Rashi. She went, adorned herself, and passed before him. He asked who she was, and she said, “Charuta,” a prostitute known in the town. He solicited her and had intercourse with her. He came home and sat in the heated oven, to kill himself. His wife told him, “It was I.” He answered, “Nevertheless, I intended a forbidden act.” He remained distressed all his life until he died through that death: Kiddushin 81b. See R. Chiyya the Great above, where it was written that he apparently was a reincarnation of Jesse, David's father. He was from Babylonia: Tosafot, Sukkah 44a. “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Ashi said: Rav said”—see there—“the mnemonic is begufa, zimra [pruning], etc.” See there. R. Abba, in his name. In Assi's name: Jerusalem Talmud, end of HaMegaresh. Rav Assi bar Natan asked him. “R. Assi said” should read “Rav said”; see R. Abba. “R. Huna said”—Beitzah 28b. If so, Rav Huna was greater than he, since he spoke in his name. But in Chullin 111b, Rav Huna and R. Chiyya bar Ashi each said to the other, “Orphan”—meaning without understanding—“did your teacher do so?” How could he call Rav Huna “orphan”? R. Zeira, in his name: Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 5, mishnah 2, and end of Elu Kesharim. Zeiri, his teacher: Yoma 77b. Zeiri's wife told him, “Your teacher ate”: Shabbat 109a, 140a. Chiyya bar Rav, his student. “R. Chisda said”—Sanhedrin 43a. “R. Yochanan said”—chapter Kol HaKelim and Pesachim 27a. R. Yitzchak son of Rabbah bar bar Chana. In Kahana's name: Jerusalem Shabbat, Kelal Gadol, halakhah 2; thus it should read: “Zeira in the name of R. Chiyya bar Ashi, in Kahana's name.” Rav Amram the Pious came before him. “Rav said”—Berakhot 42a; Kiddushin 24b, near the end; Shabbat 53a, 118b, 139b. There, 142a, “Rava said” should read “Rav.” Bekhorot 25a; see R. Abba, on the begufa mnemonic “Many times I stood before Rav to study our chapter”—Berakhot 11b, 14b. R. Chiyya bar Ashi sat before Rav and became frightened because his she-ass was about to give birth, etc.: Jerusalem Niddah, chapter 1, halakhah 4. Rava bar Abba, in his name. “Rabbah said”—HaZorek, 99b. “Shmuel said”—Chullin 127b, see there; Pesachim 30b, near the end. Rav Shmuel Sistrai, in his name. R. Shimon ben Lakish disagrees with him: Eruvin 80b, beginning.
